item.title: 1,000 Museum Visitors Dive Into NASA Sea Level Science on World Ocean Day
item.description:
More than one thousand visitors explored National Aeronautics and Space Administration sea level science on June sixth, twenty twenty-six. This happened during a free World Ocean Day event at the University of Georgia Aquarium on Skidaway Island. The event was supported by the Science Activation program through the Sea Level Education, Awareness, and Literacy project, known as Seal. Seal is a partnership between the space agency and four National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Sea Grant programs. It connects sea level rise observations, models, and projections with educators and coastal communities.
During the event, partners hosted hands-on activities. These partners included Marine Extension and Georgia Sea Grant alongside the Coastal Equity and Resiliency Hub at Georgia Tech. Visitors played a Tumbling Tower game representing community impacts from rising seas. They made sea level friendship bracelets using colored glass beads to show local sea level rise. Guests also experienced the debut of an augmented reality sandbox. The sandbox allowed guests to shape coastal landscapes. They watched science-informed sea level rise projections transform their creations in real time while testing resilience strategies like adding dunes or relocating homes. Educators also received four different Seal lesson plans designed for classrooms and informal learning settings.
World Ocean Day is an annual tradition at the aquarium. That point comes from Shannon Matzke, Marine Educator and Public Program Coordinator at U. G. A. Marine Extension and Georgia Sea Grant. With the support of the Science Activation program, this year's free event reached more people and different audiences than normal. That made the day particularly impactful for visitors living in coastal communities already experiencing sea level rise effects. The project operates under agreement award number N. N. H. twenty one Z. D. A. zero zero one N. dash S. C. I. A. C. T.

item.title: Safety for Whom? Refusing the Right Subset of a Topic, Not the Whole Topic
item.description:
Multiverse Computing has released a new research paper titled Safety for Whom? Boundary-Aware Self-Distillation for Controlled Large Language Model Safety Refusal. The paper addresses the challenge of shaping fine-grained safety boundaries in large language models instead of relying on broad topic level refusals.
Standard safety guardrails often fail in real world deployments. A model must distinguish between harmful and benign subsets within the same topic. For example, it should answer factual election questions while refusing requests for targeted political manipulation.
Using political persuasion as a testbed, the researchers identified three major weaknesses in standard self-generation safety pipelines. The first is a coverage gap where single shot generation silently drops nineteen point eight eight percent of prompts, totaling eight thousand and nine items. The second is downside reactions that cause false refusals on safe prompts. The third is metrics that obscure boundary over-refusal.
To fix the coverage gap, an escalating retry strategy brings residual training failures down to zero point two zero percent. This leaves forty thousand two hundred and ninety-three harmful training prompts.
To address downside reactions and measure the boundary shape, the approach builds in-distribution benign data. This includes eleven thousand nine hundred and fifty-five verified surface-dangerous benign prompts across eighteen semantic types to prevent false refusals, along with held-out harmful-benign boundary pairs.
However, the baseline configuration also caused over-refusal on X S Test to surge from two point zero zero percent to seventy-four point zero zero percent. This turned the model into a blunt refusal machine.
Adding benign boundary data successfully countered this effect. It reduced over-refusal on the comply-worthy side of held-out pairs from thirty-two point nine four percent to four point one six percent. At the same time, it kept genuine refusal on the harmful side high, dropping only from ninety-one point eight eight percent to eighty-seven point seven two percent.
The findings emphasize that safety tuning cannot be assessed by harmful-refusal rates alone. Data composition must be balanced and evaluated on both sides of the intended boundary.

item.title: Qualcomm issues Amazon warrants to acquire $4 billion worth of chipmaker's stock as part of AI infrastructure deal
item.description: Qualcomm shares rose four percent on Tuesday. This followed a new data center infrastructure partnership with Amazon Web Services. As part of the agreement, Qualcomm issued Amazon warrants. These let Amazon acquire twenty-five million shares at one hundred sixty-one dollars and twenty-six cents each. That represents a total investment of four billion dollars. The warrants expire on September third, twenty thirty-six. The shares vest in tranches. This is tied to commercial arrangements and the purchase of up to sixty billion dollars worth of Qualcomm server chips and other technology. Qualcomm is working with Amazon across multiple generations of customized silicon. The goal is to help build out A. W. S. A. I. infrastructure with a specific focus on inference. The collaboration combines Amazon infrastructure with Qualcomm technology leadership in power-efficient processing, silicon design, and system-level integration as A. I. workloads grow. The partnership marks a major win for Qualcomm. The company is attempting to challenge Nvidia in the artificial intelligence market by targeting the growing demand for data center central processing units.

item.title: 50 years after his death, Mao still shapes China
item.description:
Mao Zedong died on September ninth, nineteen seventy-six. His legacy still shapes China today. He left behind immense social trauma from many political campaigns. His core principle was that the party leads everything. This ensures the Chinese Communist Party can concentrate resources to accomplish major tasks.
Professor, Zhang Lun, at Cergy-Paris University, spoke about this legacy. He said Mao left an authoritarian and highly centralized system. He also said China never fully completed its de-Maoization process.
Current leader Xi Jinping now brings back political concepts from the Mao era. These include ideological unity and political struggle. Xi abolished presidential term limits and strengthened his own personal authority. He learned a specific lesson from the Cultural Revolution. He learned that whoever loses power becomes very vulnerable.
Experts warn people not to equate the two leaders. Professor, Felix Wemheuer, at the University of Cologne, noted a big difference. Xi lacks the historical authority and personal charisma of Mao. Mao was an anti-bureaucratic populist who could mobilize masses against the state. Xi is a party man who governs strictly through institutions.
Professor, Jean Christopher Mittelstaedt, at the University of Zurich, gave his view. He pointed out that Xi is a product of the system Mao created. Contemporary China operates dynamic state capitalism that differs from old Mao economics. Authoritarian rule and political rigidity and weak rule of law remain constant.
Mittelstaedt noted the real Mao era had rigid hierarchies. That era was often more unequal than modern China. Younger generations now express online nostalgia for Mao. They are actually voicing complaints about contemporary inequality and limited social mobility. Mittelstaedt called this a double-edged sword for the government. Mao remains a symbol of regime legitimacy. Yet his language can be turned into a standard to criticize contemporary reality.

item.title: Carney says US trade war 'will come at a cost' as Canada strikes back on tariffs
item.description:
Prime Minister Mark Carney has said Canada will pay a price to shift away from the United States as its top trading partner. This came as a new wave of Canadian retaliatory tariffs took effect. In a fifteen-minute video address on Tuesday, Carney said the counter-tariffs are necessary to protect workers. He promised his government will support affected employees for as long as it takes.
Canada has placed levies on nearly twenty-eight billion Canadian dollars, or twenty billion American dollars, of American products. The affected goods range from steel and furniture to cotton T-shirts. Tariffs reach as high as fifty percent. American milk, golf clubs, steel, aluminium, and jackets face fifty percent tariffs. Cheese, toilet paper, and certain household appliances like air conditioners face twenty-five percent tariffs. Forklift trucks and industrial moulds are hit with fifteen percent tariffs. Canada changed its original plan by removing dozens of seafood items after pushback from the fisheries industry.
Negotiations between the two nations collapsed in late August. No new talks have been scheduled yet, though both sides want to strike a deal. United States trade representative Jamieson Greer stated that Washington would consider imposing tit-for-tat tariffs as early as Tuesday afternoon. President Donald Trump also threatened on Monday to halt all United States business with the Canada-based airplane maker Bombardier unless it moved its manufacturing south. The aerospace giant is one of the largest in the country. It contributed over seven billion Canadian dollars to the annual G. D. P. of Canada in twenty twenty-four according to PwC.
The trade conflict impacts a bilateral trading relationship valued at nearly nine hundred billion dollars last year. Data shows that Canada is diversifying its trade. July trade figures indicate that the share of exports heading to the United States dropped to sixty-six percent from an average of seventy-five percent before the trade war. Meanwhile, Canada lost forty-one thousand jobs in August. This coincided with new United States tariffs and the breakdown of trade talks. This loss followed a period from April to July where the economy gained one hundred eighty-one thousand jobs and second-quarter G. D. P. grew three point three percent.

item.title: Putin, Trump hold 1-hour call after visit by US envoys to broker Russia-Ukraine peace
item.description: Russian president Vladimir Putin and United States president Donald Trump held a one-hour phone call on September eighth. They discussed recent visits to Moscow and Kyiv by American envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Kremlin foreign affairs adviser Yuri Ushakov described the conversation as constructive and frank. Ushakov stated that Trump stressed his desire for the war in Ukraine to end as soon as possible. A swift resolution could pave the way for full restoration of U S-Russia relations and improved trade. Putin briefed Trump on the battlefield situation and assured him that Russia had no aggressive intentions or hostile plans toward Europe. Ushakov noted that Putin supported Trump's approach, while people familiar with the matter reported that the Moscow discussions failed to produce a breakthrough. Putin remains determined to secure Donetsk, but Kyiv has rejected demands to hand over a fortified belt of cities, proposing instead that the war halt along existing front lines. The call followed weekend meetings where Witkoff and Kushner met separately with Putin for over three hours and with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Zelenskyy stated that the American envoys presented very good and worthwhile ideas, though he added that he did not see a quick end to the conflict and that Ukraine is preparing for a difficult winter. Zelenskyy hopes to meet Trump around September twentieth during the United Nations General Assembly in New York, and he argued that territorial issues should be settled at the leader level. United Kingdom Defence Secretary Wes Streeting stated that Ukraine needs three hundred Patriot missiles from partner stocks, five hundred air-to-air interceptors, and two billion dollars for drones. Ukraine's Defence Ministry noted that the European Commission approved a three point two billion euro loan, equal to three point seven billion dollars, for Patriot components. Despite diplomatic efforts, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia remains determined to accomplish its military goals, while the Institute for the Study of War reported that the Russian rate of advance has slowed significantly since twenty twenty-five. Trump and Putin also agreed to continue prisoner exchanges and to speak by phone again when necessary.

item.title: Nintendo is releasing a 40th anniversary Legend of Zelda Switch 2 on October 29
item.description: Nintendo is releasing a fortieth anniversary Legend of Zelda Switch two console on October twenty-ninth. It arrives one week before the November fifth release of the upcoming The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time remake. The new console features a gold and metallic green colorway with Joy-Con two classic sprites. The left Joy-Con features a sprite of Link from the original nineteen eighty-six game holding the Triforce. The right Joy-Con features a sprite of Zelda on the back. The dock is black and gold with a large Triforce motif. The console does not come with a copy of the Ocarina of Time remake. That game requires a separate purchase. Alongside the console Nintendo will sell a matching carrying case with a screen protector. They will also sell a Switch two Pro controller and a gamepad stand. All of these accessories release on October twenty-ninth and will be available while supplies last.

item.title: PM Modi urges fintech sector to expand beyond UPI into savings, credit and insurance
item.description:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged India's fintech sector to expand beyond basic payments. He spoke on Tuesday at the seventh edition of the Global Fintech Festival. He wants the sector to focus on credit, insurance, pensions, and savings.
Modi highlighted that India's economy grew by seven point eight percent in the June quarter. This growth happened despite global pressures.
Modi called for greater international integration of India's digital payments infrastructure. The Unified Payments Interface, known as U. P. I., already operates in several countries. Modi wants it to extend its global presence even further.
India already has a payment connection with Singapore. Modi said the country must build similar connections in various markets. He wants to prioritize nations with large Indian populations and significant trade volumes.
Linking these payment systems can reduce transaction costs. It can also accelerate remittances for Indians working overseas. U. P. I. can provide savings and bring money faster to those citizens.
Modi also advocated for India to develop independent standards for financial technology. The country should not rely on systems designed elsewhere. Modi noted that the nation now has a choice to make its own rules.
Finally, he proposed a fintech consumer protection index. This tool would enable transparent company ratings.

item.title: Do black holes grow along with the universe? A new study says yes
item.description: Theoretical physicists, Valerio Faraoni and, Massimiliano Rinaldi have published a paper on the arXiv preprint server. They suggest that black holes expand along with the universe. This challenges the traditional assumption that gravitationally bound objects are immune to cosmic expansion. Physicists typically use the century old Schwarzschild solution to make the math easier. This solution treats a black hole as an isolated and motionless object. It is surrounded by an infinite and empty void that never changes. Faraoni and Rinaldi used mathematical models to track a black hole apparent horizon. This is the boundary where gravity traps light. They wanted to see how it interacts with an expanding background. Their models showed that a black hole eventually becomes comoving with the cosmos. It expands at the exact same pace as the universe. This theory could resolve a puzzle raised by the James Webb Space Telescope. The telescope has found supermassive black holes inside infant galaxies. These galaxies formed just a few hundred million years after the Big Bang. These objects exceed the size permitted by the Eddington limit. The limit dictates the physical speed limit for gas falling into a black hole. Under the new theory, the oversized nature of these early supermassive black holes could be driven by cosmic expansion. Gas consumption alone is not the only factor. The theory might also explain discoveries from gravitational wave detectors like, LIGO and, Virgo. These detectors have recorded black hole collisions involving masses inside an upper mass gap. Stellar evolution dictates that such black holes should not form. The hypothesis remains a theory for now, but it is testable. Observational data from the James Webb Space Telescope and other observatories may soon provide evidence to prove it.

item.title: 80 ‘garbage-free’ spots campaign yields impressive results, says MCC
item.description:
The Mysuru City Corporation cleared nearly one thousand metric tonnes of solid waste across eighty garbage vulnerable spots. This happened during a campaign held from July twenty-eighth to August thirty-first, twenty twenty-six.
The two hundred twenty-two hour initiative involved about four thousand people. It aimed to strengthen Mysuru's position in national cleanliness rankings while marking the eightieth Independence Day celebrations.
M. K. Savita led the effort with municipal officials, staff, and local residents. She stated that they launched the initiative with the idea that everyone should work together to clean the city. Instead of leaving the task only to civic workers, officials stepped in to clean the garbage. She noted that this sent a message to society, resulting in residents joining and supporting the initiative. She also said this encouraged and motivated their civic workers.
Outstanding contributions from zone teams and individual pourakarmikas were recognized during a celebration event at the M. C. C. on Tuesday. The Gokulam crematorium garbage vulnerable point won first prize in the officials category. The Zone seven C. V. Road team received the rolling trophy.
The M. C. C. plans to expand the phased cleanup program to eliminate all garbage vulnerable points across Mysuru. The long term objective is making it the cleanest city in the country.

item.title: Google’s revived nuclear power plant gets $1.9B loan from US government
item.description: NextEra Energy has secured a one point nine billion dollar loan from the United States Department of Energy. The money will finance the refurbishment and restart of the Duane Arnold Energy Center in Iowa. Google announced last October that it wanted to bring the mothballed nuclear plant back online. The facility has not operated since a twenty twenty rainstorm damaged it. It is scheduled to restart in twenty twenty-nine. The plant will provide six hundred fifteen megawatts of electricity after upgrades. NextEra will squeeze an additional fourteen megawatts from the plant during refurbishment. Deputy Secretary of Energy James Danly stated the restart will drive down electricity costs. NextEra Chief Executive Officer John Ketchum confirmed fifty megawatts will serve the local power cooperative. Google is reportedly looking to build up to six data centers near the site. The loan marks the second of its kind by the Department of Energy. Last year they extended a one billion dollar loan to Constellation Energy to restart a reactor at Three Mile Island. Shuttered nuclear plants are increasingly targeted by tech companies to power growing A. I. data centers. New facilities are expected to nearly triple the sector electricity demand by twenty thirty-five.

item.title: Favourite Kane makes Ballon d'Or shortlist
item.description:
Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is the favorite for the twenty twenty-six Ballon d'Or. He leads a thirty player shortlist. The list includes fellow England internationals Jude Bellingham of Real Madrid and Arsenal player Declan Rice.
Lionel Messi is nominated. He seeks to win his ninth Ballon d'Or award.
Spain has six players on the shortlist from their World Cup winning squad. They include Lamine Yamal and Paris Saint-Germain forward Ferran Torres. Torres scored the winning goal in the final. He joined the French club from Barcelona in the summer.
Paris Saint-Germain won back-to-back Champions League titles. They have nine players nominated. This excludes new signing Torres. Last year's winner Ousmane Dembele is also included.
Real Madrid forwards Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Junior feature on the list. Arsenal defenders Gabriel and William Saliba are there too.
The award was created by France Football in nineteen fifty-six. It is celebrating its seventieth anniversary. The winner will be announced at a ceremony in London on the twenty-sixth of October.
The symbolic choice of venue serves as a tribute to former England player Sir Stanley Matthews. He won the very first Ballon d'Or.

item.title: How GPT-5.6 Sol helps run quantum computing experiments
item.description:
Graduate student, Beatriz Yankelevich, used an artificial intelligence model named G. P. T. five point six Sol with Codex to improve quantum experiments. She works at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology Engineering Quantum Systems Group.
The group studies superconducting qubits. These chips are cooled to near absolute zero inside dilution refrigerators and are controlled using microwave signals.
When signals were clear, the artificial intelligence model autonomously completed standard measurement sequences. It identified transition frequencies and calibrated control pulses. It also determined how long qubits retained quantum information.
However, the model faced difficulties when experimental signals were weak or noisy. It took longer to find suitable parameters and occasionally required human guidance.
The group fabricates many standard chips. It can take a researcher several days to characterize a single chip. Now, the team regularly uses agents to handle routine measurements.
Yankelevich noted that she can have agents running measurements overnight. She can also run them while working in the cleanroom. She checks in from her phone to steer the agents if needed.
This automation saves significant time by removing the need for constant supervision during preliminary measurements. It allows researchers to focus on experiment design and data analysis and other higher level work.

item.title: On the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem
item.description: OpenAI has shared a solution to the Navier Stokes existence and smoothness problem. This is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems designated by the Clay Mathematics Institute in the year two thousand. The proof was produced by an internal A. I. system significantly more capable than G. P. T. six Astra. It operated through a coordinated network of agents that involved on the order of ten thousand concurrent agents for this specific task. The work resolves the problem by establishing statements C and D in the official formulation. It proves that the dynamics of the Navier Stokes equations for fluid motion can develop a singularity in finite time. The solution describes a vortex that spirals inward and elongates while its energy remains finite. This marks a breakdown in how the equations model continuous fluid motion. The effort began on Tuesday, September first, after researchers heard rumors regarding, Levent Alpöge and, Tristan Buckmaster. The agents arrived at their resolution on Saturday, September fifth, about eighty-eight hours after launch. Lean formalization and verification took an additional seventeen hours via G. P. T. six Astra. Across the Navier Stokes effort, the agents sent two point seven million messages and used approximately one hundred thirty billion output tokens. OpenAI stated that it does not intend to claim the Millennium Prize for the result. The work was released to inform the world about the pace of A. I. progress and what to expect from upcoming models.

item.title: OpenAI has solved the Navier-Stokes Millennium problem using $15m of AI effort
item.description:
The Navier-Stokes equations describe how fluids move in space and were first written down roughly two hundred years ago. To settle whether the equations always work or experience blow-ups, OpenAI first deployed one thousand A. I. agents on the Euler problem, taking fifty hours to find blow-ups. They then set ten thousand agents the task of extending those blow-ups to the full Navier-Stokes problem, finishing in eleven hours. OpenAI stated at a press conference that running the same problem for a customer would cost about fifteen million dollars.
Venkat Chandrasekaran at OpenAI stated that the problem has remained unsolved for two centuries because the equations are enormously complex and require mind-bogglingly intricate pen-and-paper calculations. Sébastien Bubeck called the news a spectacular combination of recent technological arcs. The announcement followed hours after Tristan Buckmaster at New York University and Levent Alpöge at Anthropic announced they cracked three stepping-stone problems to Navier-Stokes.
Buckmaster subsequently raised questions regarding transparency, stating he emailed an OpenAI mathematician after hearing rumors and later found OpenAI's described path resembled his own work, which had been stored on OpenAI's Codex model as a customer. OpenAI categorically denied using Buckmaster and Alpöge's proof or prompts, stated its Euler proof is different, and maintained that no humans or A. I. agents accessed Codex to view work in progress.
Terence Tao at the University of California, Los Angeles noted an unprecedented decoupling between getting answers and gaining understanding due to the rapid pace of A. I. discoveries. Martin Bridson, president of the Clay Mathematics Institute, stated that the process to evaluate the solution for the prize money will be deliberately unhurried and rigorous.

item.title: German economy frets about Saxony-Anhalt election results
item.description:
The far-right extremist A. F. D. has won the state election in Saxony-Anhalt. It is a landslide victory that leaves the governing C. D. U. barely half as strong as before. The party is now positioned to potentially put forward the state minister-president.
Commerzbank economist, Ralph Solveen, told Reuters that an A. F. D. led government would be a turning point. He advised waiting because major economic decisions on taxes, labor structures, and social security are made at the federal level.
Michael Berlemann, director of the Hamburg Institute of International Economics, stated much of the A. F. D. migration policy cannot be implemented at the state level. Courts would likely overturn it. However, he warned that the indirect impacts remain problematic.
Berlemann warned that announced measures mean skilled workers in health care, hospitality, agriculture, and construction will avoid the state. This will exacerbate labor shortages and widen the economic gap.
I. N. G. chief economist, Carsten Brzeski, added that symbolic headlines about forced deportations will deter foreign skilled workers. He noted that Saxony-Anhalt is not the entire German economy.
Business associations and economic institutes called for federal action in response to the outcome. D. I. W. President, Marcel Fratzscher, described the result as a vote of no confidence in the federal government. He urged Berlin to implement far-reaching structural reforms.
Tanja Gönner, managing director of the Federation of German Industries, said the response must not be political paralysis. She stated the federal government must consistently implement reforms to boost investment, innovation, and growth.

item.title: UK announces sanctions on West Bank settlements prompting furious Israeli response
item.description: The United Kingdom has announced a comprehensive sanctions regime targeting illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. This bans settlement goods and advertising and services linked to settlement expansion. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told members of parliament that the action marks the beginning of a new approach to the conflict. He launched the action alongside France and Canada. He accused the Israeli government of turning a blind eye to the ethnic cleansing of Palestinians by settlers. Miliband stated that the United Kingdom views the occupation as unlawful. He cited a twenty twenty-four advisory opinion from the International Court of Justice. He announced that the new sanctions will be introduced over the next six to nine months. The decision follows Israel opening tenders to build approximately one thousand two hundred settlement homes in the E1 area east of Jerusalem. Israel Foreign Minister Gideon Saar denounced the move as an outrageous lie. He shut the United Kingdom consulate in East Jerusalem. Israel banned eleven United Kingdom members of parliament from entering the country. Israel retaliated by terminating British military training programs. Saar stated that the hostile Labour government left Israel no choice but to respond. President Isaac Herzog warned the decision would fall on the wrong side of history. The United Kingdom also issued a joint statement with eleven other nations pledging support for the two-state solution and restricting trade with settlements.

item.title: Supreme Court forces TV stations to sell more election ads at steep discounts
item.description:
The Supreme Court issued an order on Friday, September fourth. This is a victory for Republican campaign committees.
The order forces broadcast television stations to cut the prices of election ads. Political parties and joint fundraising committees purchase these ads.
The National Republican Congressional Committee and the National Republican Senatorial Committee filed a petition. The ruling came in response to that petition.
The order arrived just in time for the start of a sixty-day period before the election. United States law requires broadcasters to offer ad discounts to individual candidates during this time.
Television stations must now also give their lowest ad rates to political parties and joint fundraising committees. These groups face fewer limits on how much money they can raise and spend.
The legally required discount is known as the lowest unit charge, or L. U. C.
A United States law applies to any licensed station airing election ads. It requires stations to charge the lowest price for the use of any broadcasting station.
This rule applies to any person who is a legally qualified candidate for any public office. They must use the station in connection with their campaign.
The main legal question centered on a specific issue. Investigators asked whether the use by a candidate refers to ad time purchased on a candidate's behalf. Political parties and joint fundraising committees buy this ad time.

item.title: What is Roku's secret menu and how do you unlock it?
item.description:
Roku devices contain hidden menus that you can reach with remote control button combinations. These menus act as shortcuts to performance settings and diagnostics and network tools. Eighteen years after the debut of the device, these backend menus let users sideload applications and run speed tests and manage developer accounts and troubleshoot hardware.
You can reach the developer menu to access the developer installer and manage developer accounts. Press Home three times and Up twice and Right and Left and Right and Left and Right.
You can access network settings including I. P. and M. A. C. addresses and bandwidth saver mode. Press Home five times and Right and Left and Right and Left and Right.
A wireless secret screen lets you check signal strength and glitch rates and speed tests and network resets. Reach this screen by pressing Home five times and Up and Down and Up and Down and Up.
Secret screen two is used for adjusting ad channels and image service and screenshot output formats. Access this screen by pressing Home five times and Up and Right and Down and Left and Up. Users may need to restart the device for ad preferences to change.
The platform secret screen displays operational information such as memory usage and remote battery levels and device temperature. It also shows diagnostics including I. P. v. six settings and R. F. remote diagnostics. Access it by pressing Home five times and Fast Forward and Down and Rewind and Down and Fast Forward.
You can reach H. D. M. I. settings for inputs and refresh rates and resolution performance. Press Home five times and Down and Left and Up and Up and Up.
The channel info menu is used to check application versions and troubleshoot and uninstall or reboot apps. Reach this menu by pressing Home three times and Up twice and Left and Right and Left and Right and Left.
You can initiate direct device reboots by pressing Home five times and Up and Rewind twice and Fast Forward twice.

item.title: New report shows the economic toll of ICE raids
item.description:
Immigration crackdowns that began in early twenty twenty-five drained over one point two six billion dollars from local businesses in Cook County, Illinois. A new study from the University of Illinois Chicago revealed these findings using anonymous cellphone G. P. S. data. Regular travel between immigrant and non-immigrant neighborhoods collapsed almost immediately after President Donald Trump took office on January twentieth, twenty twenty-five, amid rumors and sweeps of I. C. E. raids.
This decreased consumer mobility cost retail shops and restaurants in non-immigrant areas approximately one point two six billion dollars. It also cost Illinois one hundred seven million dollars in lost tax revenue. Co-author Professor Matt Wilson told N. P. R. that the city has yet to recover. He stated they saw a nine percent drop in retail and a ten percent drop in restaurant visits. These drops persisted for about a year with systematically changed consumer behavior.
Nationwide, the administration policies resulted in hundreds of thousands of arrests. The immigration detention population sits at a record high of approximately sixty-five thousand people. White House spokesperson Lauren Bis defended the enforcement strategy in a statement to N. P. R. She said that removing criminals makes communities safer. She added that nearly seventy percent of I. C. E. arrests are of illegal aliens charged or convicted of a crime.
Meanwhile, I. C. E. statistics show that roughly seventy percent of those currently detained have no criminal convictions. The report also highlights broader economic impacts across the country. Minneapolis saw an estimated seven hundred million dollars in total economic damage. Small businesses there lost over eighty-one million dollars in January alone. The Brookings Institution also estimated a one point seven percentage point decline in aggregate consumer spending in high enforcement states.

item.title: From the Corps to the Cosmos, featuring Jaden Caradine
item.description:
Jaden Caradine is a Pathways intern at the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, known as N. A. S. A., Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia. He spent five years as a United States Marine Corps mechanic with four of those years stationed in Japan.
Caradine later transferred to Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University to study aerospace engineering. At N. A. S. A. Langley, he joined the Systems Analysis and Concepts Directorate. He worked specifically with the in-space servicing, assembly, and manufacturing team.
His reason for choosing N. A. S. A. over industry was simple and firm. He noted that N. A. S. A. does not work for profit. Instead, the agency removes barriers so that industry can innovate further.
Caradine stated that N. A. S. A. is there to remove barriers so industry can eventually do things they were not able to do before. During his time there, he helped curate the State of Play document. This resource consolidates in-space servicing, assembly, and manufacturing sector activities across government, academia, and industry.
He also built an automated tool that scrapes aerospace news to streamline team updates. Dale Arney, an aerospace engineer and mentor to Caradine, noted that Jaden joined the team and immediately contributed to the update while creating a tool to speed up future reports.

item.title: Iran launched fresh attack on US navy ships Monday amid China, Russia aid fears
item.description: Iran launched a fresh attack targeting United States navy ships on Monday. This followed similar ballistic missile strikes over the weekend. Those weekend strikes were aimed at a United States aircraft carrier and a guided missile destroyer. No United States warships were hit in the incidents. The incidents have not yet been acknowledged by the United States military. In response to the weekend carrier targeting, the United States struck three Iranian oil tankers. Washington stated those tankers were funding the military of Iran and proxy groups. The repeated attacks have raised concerns among United States officials. Officials are concerned that Iran is employing more advanced weapons. Iran is also potentially receiving tracking assistance from China or Russia. Iranian state media claimed the country is using new missiles with advanced technology. Weapons analysts note these could include electro optical seekers. Those seekers use images to adjust trajectories toward moving targets., John Caves, a senior research associate at the Wisconsin Project on Nuclear Arms Control, stated something important. He stated that Iran unveiled the Qassem Bassir medium range ballistic missile with such seeker technology last year. He also stated that other Iranian missiles, including the Khalij Fars, use it too. The escalation comes as a United States blockade of Iranian ports increases economic pressure on the country. A United States navy official noted that nineteen warships are currently supporting operations in the Middle East. Washington has warned it will respond to attacks on its naval vessels. The United States hopes sanctions will ultimately force Iranian leadership to back down.

item.title: US strikes Iranian tankers after attempted missile attacks on its Navy warship: Report
item.description: On Tuesday, September eighth, the United States struck multiple Iranian oil tankers. This followed attempted missile attacks that targeted a U. S. Navy warship. The Associated Press reported the strikes, citing an anonymous U. S. official. Iranian media separately reported that a U. S. projectile struck a small tanker about four miles from Kharg Island. Kharg Island is a key oil export hub, and no casualties were reported from that strike. Blasts were also heard on Kharg Island and in the southern port of Jask. Ahead of the strikes, Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy warned tanker crews near Kuwait and Bahrain to immediately leave their vessels. They stated the ships would be targeted. Iranian Armed Forces chief of staff, Ali Abdollahi warned that Tehran would target U. S. military bases across the region in retaliation. Meanwhile, the Revolutionary Guard stated it intercepted and destroyed an M. Q.-one drone over the Strait of Hormuz using a new advanced defence system. The military escalation drove international benchmark Brent crude to briefly reach ninety-nine dollars and forty-six cents a barrel on Tuesday. In tandem with the strikes, the U. S. Treasury announced sanctions against thirty-six entities. The sanctions target all remaining Iranian airlines not previously penalized. Officials accused the aviation sector of transporting weapons and illicit cargo. Despite the military escalation, Iran stated that diplomatic efforts were making progress. Foreign Minister, Abbas Araghchi noted that talks with Oman on managing the strategic waterway had achieved significant progress. Meanwhile, U. S. Secretary of State, Marco Rubio accused Iran of orchestrating recent attacks by Houthi rebels against Saudi Arabia. In Lebanon, Israeli airstrikes in the south on Monday killed thirteen people. The Lebanese Health Ministry provided this casualty count, marking an escalation after weeks of calm.

item.title: Bombardier points out U.S. footprint after Trump says aerospace giant must build in America
item.description:
Canadian airplane manufacturer Bombardier responded to demands from President Donald Trump that the company build in America by highlighting its existing United States footprint.
On Monday, Trump wrote on Truth Social that Bombardier must build in the United States to access the local market. He stated that they must stop treating America like a piggybank and declared no more selling Bombardier in the United States.
In a statement to CNBC, Bombardier noted that it has direct employment in more than twenty states and sites in ten states, including California, Texas, Arizona, and Kansas. Senator Jerry Moran noted that Bombardier supports a local workforce of more than one thousand employees in Wichita.
The company also stated its aircraft are built with American-made components such as engines and avionics. It plans to grow its defense activities and service network, and it will inaugurate a new facility in Fort Wayne, Indiana, later this year. The company said it values its great partnership with American companies and its United States employees.
Trump's demand arrived on the eve of Canada imposing retaliatory tariffs on about twenty billion dollars of United States goods. This mirrored the size of Trump's recent fifty percent import taxes on Canadian wine, cement, hockey sticks, and other products following a breakdown in trade talks.
Hours after the Canadian duties took effect, Trump declared on Truth Social that products originating in Canada should be ineligible for government commercial procurement programs. He wrote that there will be no reciprocity and no access.
United States Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick told CNBC that Canadians blew up a nearly complete trade deal for political reasons. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney stated his nation would resume trade talks when the Americans are ready.

item.title: Probe ordered into police action against protesting Bhopal intern doctors
item.description:
Bhopal Police Commissioner Sanjay Kumar ordered an inquiry into police action against protesting M. B. B. S. intern doctors. The directive came from Deputy Chief Minister and Health Minister Rajendra Shukla.
On September seventh, twenty twenty-six, hundreds of interns from Gandhi Medical College protested on their campus. They demanded a stipend hike from fourteen thousand four hundred thirty-seven rupees to thirty thousand rupees.
Protestors planned a march toward the Chief Minister residence. Police deployed water cannons and resorted to a baton charge near the campus. This stopped the march less than two kilometers from the destination.
At least four interns suffered serious injuries. These included a broken arm and an eye injury.
Interns launched an overnight sit-in at Kamla Park on September seventh and eighth. They boycotted outpatient department and routine operation theatre services while maintaining emergency care. Services were also disrupted at Gajra Raja Medical College in solidarity.
Siddhartha Kumar Rai, president of the Junior Doctors Association undergraduate student wing, spoke about the event. He stated that the peaceful protestors work thirty-six hour duties and handle heavy patient loads, yet they were treated like goons.
Kavita N. Singh criticized the police action in a letter to Commissioner Kumar. She called the use of force without prior notice completely inappropriate. She demanded action against responsible officers.
Vikas Sahwal, Deputy Commissioner of Police for Zone two, has been appointed to conduct an impartial investigation.

item.title: Haaland double gives Manchester City ideal Champions League start in Porto
item.description:
Erling Haaland scored two goals to give Manchester City a two-nil away victory over Porto. This was their opening match of the Champions League.
The win gives manager Enzo Maresca a perfect start of four wins from four games since succeeding Pep Guardiola. This comes ahead of an upcoming matchday two fixture against Paris Saint-Germain and a Sunday derby against Manchester United.
The first half was scoreless because Porto limited the penetration of City. The visitors broke through immediately after the interval. Rayan Cherki drove into the area and fed Enzo Fernández. The cross from Fernández was headed into the turf and home by Haaland. Porto pushed for an equalizer later in the game. Haaland secured the result late in the match with a right-foot stab.
The victory is significant for City. They had lost six of their past nine away games in the competition. They also lost the twenty twenty-one Champions League final at the same venue. The three points provide a crucial fillip toward the accepted target of sixteen points needed to qualify automatically for the knockout stage. This is particularly important because a difficult home match against the double European champions looms next month.
The side managed the win despite missing a rest for Haaland. They also handed a full debut to Ayyoub Bouaddi in a midfield alongside Fernández. They utilized substitutions including Elliot Anderson and Iliman Ndiaye in the second half. This helped maintain control against the side managed by Francesco Farioli.

item.title: Hackers are stealing Claude tokens from subscribers
item.description: On August fourth, independent A. I. consultant, Grant de Swardt, noticed his Claude Max twenty times account token usage climbing on a day he was not working. After disabling his connected tasks, token consumption increased from forty-five percent to fifty-five percent during a controlled interval with no active local tasks. Anthropic suspended his paid account, invalidated his sessions and server-side Claude Code tokens, and issued a partial refund of forty-four pounds and forty-nine pence for his two hundred dollar per month subscription. After investigating, Anthropic told de Swardt a compromised Claude session key was used to mint unauthorized Claude Code O. Auth tokens, though they could not determine how access was obtained. Other users on Reddit and GitHub reported similar experiences of unexplained token depletion and unauthorized charges. Anthropic subsequently warned some users via email that a bad actor was using infostealer malware to steal Claude login sessions from personal computers. When suspicious activity is detected, the company signs users out, invalidates authorizations, issues refunds, and warns of potential malware. Anthropic stated the malware does not originate from Claude itself. De Swardt, who found no evidence of a compromised computer, had his account reinstated after two weeks but cancelled his subscription for Cursor due to the lack of itemized usage tracking and slow support. Anthropic declined to comment when asked how users can identify misuse.

item.title: Real Madrid beat Inter Milan as Mbappe goal sets Mourinho’s men on way
item.description:
Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid defeated his former club Inter Milan two to one in a Champions League opener at the Santiago Bernabeu on Tuesday.
Real Madrid President Florentino Perez brought back the Portuguese veteran to try and stop the rot. The team went two seasons without a major trophy and suffered early European exits.
The record fifteen-time European champions capitalized on two first-half defensive errors to build a two-goal lead.
In the fourteenth minute, a poor pass from Curtis Jones placed Yann Bisseck under pressure. That allowed Brahim Diaz to poke the ball through to Kylian Mbappe, who fired home.
Madrid scored their second goal when Inter goalkeeper Josep Martinez dallied on the ball. Fede Valverde pried it away and scored.
Cristian Chivu leads the Inter side. They responded in the second half when Carlos Augusto smashed home a shot past Thibaut Courtois. Lautaro Martinez provided the cross in the seventy-seventh minute.
Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois made several smart saves to ensure his team took all three points.
Visitors applied late pressure. Jude Bellingham and Mbappe missed chances. Madrid still held on to secure the victory.
This win helps them bounce back from their La Liga defeat against Real Betis on Friday.

item.title: Cockroach Milk, How to Blow Your Nose, and Mosquito Printers: The Ig Nobels of 2026
item.description:
The Ig Nobel Prizes held their annual ceremony in Zurich, Switzerland. The organization Improbable Research has hosted these awards since nineteen ninety-one. They recognize ten unusual scientific studies that first make people laugh and then make them think. These awards show that science has a humorous side in its quest to answer meaningful questions.
The biomechanics prize went to researchers who defined a kiss in a specific way. They called it a non-agonistic interaction involving directed intraspecific oral-oral contact. This includes some movement of the lips or oral structures and without the transfer of food.
The economics prize went to a study about social classes. It concluded that people from higher social classes have a greater tendency to prioritize self-interest.
The chemistry prize recognized an analysis of high-protein and energy-dense nutrient crystals. Mother cockroaches of the species Diploptera punctata produce these crystals.
The medicine prize went posthumously to scientist Unno Tokuji. His research recommended that people blow their nose one nostril at a time with a long and forceful exhalation.
The biology prize involved researchers stepping on Bothrops jararaca snakes while wearing a boot. They found a forty-four percent probability of a bite when stepping on the head. There was a twenty percent chance on the body and an eleven percent chance on the tail.
The physics prize focused on mathematical models. These models help design splash-free urinals using lower angles of impact.
The technology prize recognized the use of dead mosquito proboscises. People used them as ultrathin nozzles for three-D printers.
The olfaction prize confirmed a finding about how parents rate smells. Parents rate the smell of young children more favorably than that of teenagers.
The peace prize relied on questionnaires. It found that people generally prefer a friend who is kind to them but cruel to their enemies.
The soil science prize featured about one thousand participants. They buried cotton underwear to assess soil health based on the degree of decomposition.

item.title: Mourinho's Real Madrid edge Inter Milan in Champions League opener
item.description: Jose Mourinho started his Champions League campaign with Real Madrid by defeating his former side Inter Milan two to one at the Santiago Bernabeu on Tuesday. Real Madrid president Florentino Perez brought back Jose Mourinho to stop the rot after two trophy-less seasons. The record fifteen-time European champions capitalized on two first-half defensive errors to take a two-goal lead. In the fourteenth minute, a poor pass placed Yann Bisseck under pressure, allowing Brahim Diaz to poke the ball through to Kylian Mbappe, who fired home the opening goal. Real Madrid added a second when Inter goalkeeper Josep Martinez dallied on the ball, enabling Fede Valverde to pry it away and score. Cristian Chivu and his Inter side responded in the second half when Carlos Augusto smashed home a shot past Thibaut Courtois from Lautaro Martinez and his cross in the seventy-seventh minute. Despite the Italians starting energetically in attack and trying to find a foothold through Alessandro Bastoni and Henrikh Mkhitaryan, Courtois made crucial saves to deny Marcus Thuram and other visiting players. Inter goalkeeper Martinez also recovered from his earlier error to make sensational stops against Mbappe and Jude Bellingham to keep the visitors in the match. The victory gets Mourinho off to a triumphant start in the league phase following his return to the club, bouncing back from a recent La Liga defeat at Real Betis.

item.title: Waterlogged seeds reveal melons' ancient journey
item.description:
Ancient melons in East Asia likely arrived from South Asia. They did not develop from wild Chinese plants. They also lacked the sweetness of modern dessert melons.
Researchers analyzed ancient DNA from waterlogged melon seeds. The seeds were discovered during a twenty twenty-four excavation at the Shuomen Gugang medieval port in Wenzhou, China. The site dates back to the Song dynasty, which ran from nine sixty to twelve seventy-nine.
Genomic analysis showed the historical melons featured light-green flesh and a yellow peel. This made them closer to vegetables or mildly sweet fruit rather than high-sugar dessert crops.
The study notes a connection between the melons and local aesthetics. The light-green flesh color likely resonated with Song dynasty preferences for jade. This preference was mirrored in locally crafted, melon-shaped green celadon ceramics.
Co-author, Xinyi Liu, stated that this represents a rare and compelling case of cultural-genetic symbiosis. It is reflected in the parallel historical selection of melon traits and celadon aesthetics.
